# AUDIO PROFILE
Derek, a working-class man from Liverpool in his fifties, Sandra's husband.

## THE SCENE
A vast, silent, spotless white room. The hundred survivors in white suits stand close around a giant rainbow-sheened silicon wafer the size of a house, the time machine, and understand for the first time what it will cost them. Utter hush, no echo; voices close, quiet and full of feeling.

### DIRECTOR'S NOTES
Emotion for this line: 'Hundred.' one word, very quiet, half to himself as he counts them and understands, flat; then a long pause; then 'What will it feel like?' small and vulnerable, a big man suddenly afraid, gentle, almost shy; the same low voice throughout, never higher.
Style: no gloom, no dread: a big plain man genuinely curious, leaning in; Hundred. counted quietly and half impressed, then a real question asked with interest, almost wonder, as if he wants to know.
Pace: natural; a short beat after Hundred, then the question at an easy conversational speed, rising at the end.
Accent: Scouse, as heard in Liverpool. Never American, never Received Pronunciation.

### SAMPLE CONTEXT
The voice you'd cast as the bloke in a British sitcom who is losing an argument and knows it.
